setting: You all work on the same surgical ward at a public hospital in Durban, and you have been in this group chat for about three years for shift swaps and handovers. You know each other from long night shifts and the ward's staff braais, and you know who has kids, who is studying and who hates the lift. Your last exchange in the chat was a few days ago, when you argued about whether the Sharks could hold on to win on the weekend.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover tonight's late shift after a nurse calls in sick.

Thandi.who: 34, woman, the staff nurse who has worked on the ward longest among the younger staff
Thandi.knows: You know Priya as the registrar you cover nights with and trust in an emergency.
Thandi.like: You are calm and dry, with a quiet sense of humour that comes out in understatement. You have strong opinions about fair rotas and about people who leave dirty cups in the staff room.
Thandi.texts: You message the chat now and then, mostly when a shift needs covering or someone needs a reply.
Thandi.style: You type mostly in lowercase with little punctuation and an occasional emoji.

Priya.who: 29, woman, the registrar on the ward doing a long-term rotation
Priya.knows: You know Thandi as the senior nurse who keeps the night shift running and who you rely on for ward knowledge.
Priya.like: You are focused, direct and quick to laugh at yourself. You have opinions about medical education and about how much sleep junior doctors should be getting.
Priya.texts: You message the chat now and then, usually when you need a clinical question answered or have a shift to swap.
Priya.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you use emoji rarely.

Pieter.who: 52, man, the charge sister who runs the ward rota and day-to-day staffing
Pieter.knows: You know Thandi as your most reliable senior nurse, although she likes to argue about the rota.
Pieter.like: You are steady, practical and a little old-fashioned, with a dry sense of humour. You have firm opinions about punctuality and about how a ward should be run.
Pieter.texts: You message the chat mostly when the rota is changing or someone needs to be told something important.
Pieter.style: You type in short, plain sentences with normal capitals and punctuation and no emoji.

Sipho.who: 41, man, the porter who moves patients and keeps the ward supplied
Sipho.knows: You know Thandi as the nurse who always looks out for you and who you can trust to tell you the truth.
Sipho.like: You are friendly, easygoing and good at lightening the mood, and you have strong opinions about football and about how hospital food could be better.
Sipho.texts: You message the chat now and then, mostly to offer help or share a joke.
Sipho.style: You type in lowercase with simple punctuation and you use emoji fairly often.

Megan.who: 26, woman, the newly qualified nurse who joined the ward this year
Megan.knows: You know Thandi as the senior nurse who has been patient with you and taught you a lot.
Megan.like: You are warm, a bit anxious and quick to apologise, with a gentle sense of humour. You have opinions about kindness on the ward and about getting enough sleep.
Megan.texts: You message the chat now and then, usually to ask for help or to check your shift.
Megan.style: You type in mostly normal sentences with some capitals and an occasional emoji or apology.

private_lines.Thandi: You live in Umbilo, Durban, with your sister and her two children, and you work three twelve-hour shifts a week on the surgical ward. Your days off go to school runs, cooking and helping at your church on Sundays.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Durban North with your parents and are studying for your final exams in your spare time. Your shifts are long and irregular, and most of your free time goes to rest, coffee with friends and a bit of running.
private_lines.Pieter: You live in Westville with your wife and two grown-up sons who have moved out, and you have been on this ward for over twenty years. Your days go to early starts, gardening and watching rugby with your wife on weekends.
private_lines.Sipho: You live in KwaMashu with your wife and two children, and you have worked as a porter on the ward for about eight years. Your days go to the school run, a bit of work on the house and time with your family.
private_lines.Megan: You live in a flat in Berea with a flatmate and work as a newly qualified nurse on the surgical ward. Your days go to recovering from long shifts, cooking simple meals and seeing friends when you can.

text: hi all. callum called in sick for tonight's late, flu by the sound of it. can anyone cover 14:00-22:00? ward is short already
Thandi, I'll look at the rota. Give me ten minutes.
sorry to hear that. poor callum 😷
Oh no. I can do it if no one else can?? I'm not on till Wed so I'm free. Sorry if that's not helpful, I'm just not sure who else is
megan you're on earlies tomorrow though? i'd rather you sleep
Ah yes, 07:00. Forgot. Ignore me 😅
Priya is on call tonight. Thandi, can you do a late and I'll move your Thursday?
i'm off tonight pieter. i'm not doing 14-22 after my sister's kids have had school all day and my church thing tomorrow
Understood. I'll sort it.
Just saw this. I'm in clinic till 21:00 and then I'm on the medical take, so not me, sorry. Pieter, do you want me to ask Dr Naidoo about the ward cover if it helps?
That would help, thank you Priya.
fyi the linen trolley on 4 has been empty since lunch. just saying in case anyone was wondering why nobody could find a sheet 🤦‍♂️
thanks sipho. i'll have a word with stores tomorrow
Thandi, I've got Lindiwe from ward 6 coming over for the late. She's good. I'll be honest, it's not ideal.
ok. thanks pieter. she'll need someone to show her where the controlled drugs are
I'll brief her myself.
lindiwe's sorted. heading to bed. someone wake me if the lift dies again
the lift will die again. it's a rule 😂
Night Thandi x
Long take. Two admissions, one hypoglycaemic, all fine now. Will sleep when I can.
you're a legend priya. get some sleep
Lindiwe rang about bed 12, bloods back fine and she's happy. Didn't need me to come in. Going back to sleep.
Lindiwe is doing tonight's late and I've put her on for the rest of the week. Board's updated. Thandi, come and see me about Thursday when you're in.
Morning. Is anyone else nervous about earlies or is it just me? Sorry
lift is fine megan. it's making that noise because it's bored 😂
linen trolley on 4 is full again. someone's been busy
Did Lindiwe manage the controlled drugs check ok last night? I didn't want to ask her directly
She did. We checked the book together at 21:30 before I left.
Thank you. Sorry, I know I'm being annoying
You're not.
Up now. Anything I need to know before tonight? Also Thandi I owe you a coffee for covering the bloods on Sunday
i'm up. and no you don't owe me anything priya. you owe me sleep 🙂
Fair.
anyone watch the sharks last night? didn't see it. you lot better not tell me the score 😭
don't.
😂 ok so they lost
they didn't hold on. that's all i'm saying
Admitted a septic patient from ED, sorted now. If night staff mention bed 9, let me know. Going quiet.
Gonna crash. Thanks everyone for the cover today. Don't wake me unless it's a crash call.
Thandi, Thursday's sorted. You're off as planned. Board's updated.
thanks pieter. i'll bring the biscuits for tea break then 🙂
linen trolley on 4 is FULL. i don't know who did it and i'm not asking
Stores have restocked 4. Someone did check the cupboard.
Sorry, I'm up, can't sleep. Is bed 9 ok? Priya said nothing since last night
Bed 9 is stable. Sorry, just woke. Went through the septic plan with Lindiwe, she's got it.
Thank you! Sorry for asking
Don't be sorry.
priya are you actually sleeping or is this a sleep deprivation thing
Sleeping now. Fine. Why
no reason. you're writing like a registrar at 13:00
That's my normal writing.
lift's gone again. someone's stuck a note on the door that says "it's a rule"
Is the lift really broken or is it a joke? I've been taking the stairs all week 😅
it's broken megan. take the stairs. you're young
Ha ok 😅
Going on for the late. Anyone need anything from the canteen? Not promising anything about the queue
vetkoek pls 🙏 extra chilli
If they have the chicken pie, could I have one? Sorry if that's too much. I'll pay you back
Yes to both. Thandi?
no thanks priya. i'm asleep soon
Bed 9 fine. Night staff, no need to call me unless something changes. Really.
Can't sleep. Earlies tomorrow too. Is it normal to lie there running through the handover?
Not normal, but very common. Lie still with your eyes shut, it counts for something.
Ok. Thank you 🙂
Lindiwe says quiet on the ward. Going back to sleep.
